result:
I've written the plan for w210 (supervision r135 and r136) at `.shop/scratch/3-plan/plan.md`, and the result file says DONE with no open questions. It builds on the first plan, and the answers of 2026-10-27 settle that plan's two questions.

- **r135, raising the lines:** a new `scripts/supervise_raise.py` raises each upstream entry of an integrate round's result with `work request`. It runs in the upstream's repository, raised for the request the initiative fulfils and passing that request's delegation when it has one. For that, w210 also adds `--raised-for` to `work request` (requests r29), since no other work-item covers it.
- **The record:** each raised request adds a line to `raised.jsonl`, which names the integrate round it came from. It goes into the same commit as the round's proposals.
- **Order at the end of the integrate round:** the existing change-list checks (r96, r107) come first, then the raise, then the proposals and one commit.
- **When a raise fails (answer C):**
  - `work run` writes no proposal and commits or pushes nothing from the round.
  - The initiative branch is left as it was before the round, and `.shop/work/` is left as its last commit has it.
  - It exits with an error naming the round, the upstream and `work`'s reason, and the round runs again next time (r93).
  - Today the round's branch is merged before its result is read. The implementer can either move the raise ahead of that merge or undo the merge when the raise fails.
- **r136, holding the proposal:** `draft_proposals` skips a formulated proposal whose integrate round raised a request that the upstream doesn't show as delivered. If that request can't be read at all, the proposal is held (answer A).
- **One existing test needs rewriting:** the spec-integration @r44 scenario raises into `../billing-ctx`, which is only a spec directory. Under the new behaviour that raise would fail, so its setup has to make `../billing-ctx` a real repository that keeps requests. This is reasoned, not run: that scenario can't be collected under `--work-item w210`.

The plan leaves several cases for the implementer to name. The most notable: when a round raises into two upstreams and the second fails, the first request already exists upstream, and the next run will raise it again.
